case_name: State of Karnataka v K. Gopalakrishna
respondent:
K. Gopalakrishna
Supreme Court of India

18 January 2005
Appeal (Crl.) 1204 of 1999
The Judgment was delivered by : B. P. Singh, J.
1.  This appeal by special leave has been preferred by the State of Karnataka against the Judgment and Order of the High Court of Karnataka at Bangalore dated December 18, 1998 in Criminal Appeal No.640 of 1996 whereby the appeal preferred by the respondent herein was allowed and he was acquitted of all the charges levelled against him. The respondent was tried by the Principal Sessions Judge, Belgaum in Sessions Case No.62 of 1994 charged of offences under Sections 302, 201 and 498A IPC, and alternatively under Section 304B IPC. The learned Sessions Judge by his Judgment and Order dated 27.6.1996 found the respondent guilty of the offence under Section 302 IPC and sentenced him to undergo imprisonment for life. He also found him guilty of the offence under Section 201 IPC for which he was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for
facts: The case of the prosecution is that the respondent strangulated to death his wife Veena and thereafter set her on fire along with her infant child aged a year and a half.
An occurrence is said to have taken place in the morning of 22nd November, 1993.
The deceased Veena was the daughter of Laxmamma (PW1) and was married to the respondent on June 3, 1991.
A male child was born to the couple on March 7, 1992.
On or about 25.10.1993 he came to the house of his mother-in-law at Shimoga and took away his wife Veena to Nesargi.
The case of the prosecution is that despite the request made to the respondent, he refused to attend the marriage ceremony of Vijaya (PW11).
Four days thereafter, on 22.11.1993 the occurrence took place in which Veena as well as her child lost their lives.
issues: Whether the respondent was guilty of the offence under Section 302 IPC and other charges levelled against him.
Whether the evidence of prosecution witnesses who deposed to the existence of motive were reliable or not.
petitioner_arguments: The respondent used to ill treat his wife Veena and used to pressurise her to get money from her mother.
There was a quarrel between the deceased and the respondent an hour before the occurrence, and soon thereafter the occurrence took place.
court_reasoning: The Trial Court relying upon the evidence of prosecution witnesses came to the conclusion that the respondent was ill treating his wife and was making demands of money and had the motive to commit the offence.

The High Court has considered the evidence on record and reached the conclusion that the prosecution witnesses who deposed to the existence of motive were not reliable and their evidence was inconsistent.
holding: We find this approach to be wholly unreasonable. Apart from the fact that the respondent used to press the deceased to get money from her mother, there is also clear evidence on record to establish the fact that she was being ill treated by the respondent.
The evidence in that regard is consistent and has been deposed to by a large number of witnesses, some of whom were family members and others were the residents of Shimoga and were family friends.
